qs.q: A 28-year-old woman with recurrent urinary tract infections presents with right flank pain, fever, and costovertebral angle tenderness. What is the most frequent route of bacterial entry causing this renal infection?
qs.e: Bacteria predominantly ascend from the lower urinary tract to cause acute pyelonephritis. Hematogenous seeding occurs less frequently, typically from systemic bacteremia.
